newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Burundi army rules out any war with Tanzania.
newsitem.headline: Burundi army rules out any war with Tanzania.

text.p: The Burundian army ruled out on Monday the possibility of it going to war with neighbouring Tanzania, from where Burundian Hutu rebels are infiltrating into Burundi.
"There is no military problem between Tanzania and Burundi," said army spokesman Lieutenant-Colonel Isaie Nibizi.
He said Hutu rebel were attacking southern Burundi from northwest Tanzania but the Tanzanian army was not involved.
"There are regular contacts between military authorities in Tanzania and Burundi," said Nibizi.
He added that military relations were good between the two countries.
He said south Burundi was "becoming calm" but a major road along Lake Tanganyika was closed because of insecurity there.
Burundian Hutu rebels of the National Council for the Defence of Democracy were uprooted from their bases in Zaire last year when Zairean Tutsi-dominated rebels seized the area.
They then shifted their main base of operations to Tanzania, from where Burundi's defence minister said last week more than 2,000 Hutu rebels had attacked this month.

Tanzania and its former president Julius Nyerere, the international mediator on Burundi, backed regional sanctions against Burundi imposed shortly after Pierre Buyoya seized power in a coup by the country's Tutsi-dominated army last July.
But the embargo, which was eased this month, benefitted Tanzania as smuggling picked up while other routes were blocked.
More than 150,000 people, mostly civilians, have been killed in massacres and civil war between the Tutsi-dominated army and rebels since troops killed Burundi's Hutu president in 1993.
